candidates.attacker_control: The label is a URL path variable on ResourceController ("/{name}/{profile}/{label}/**", lines 71-78/132-137) and on EnvironmentController ("/{name}/{profiles}/{label:.*}", lines 108-121). Using the documented "(_)" encoding (replace with "/" in ResourceController.resolveLabel and EnvironmentController.labelled) an attacker can place '/' and '..' inside one label segment, so the raw request line contains no normalizable "../" segment while the repository sees a traversing label such as master/../../../../etc. The requested resource filename (path variable after the label) is also attacker-controlled.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The relative resource path IS strongly validated: GenericResourceRepository.isInvalidPath rejects ".." paths after StringUtils.cleanPath and URL/"url:" paths, and isInvalidEncodedPath additionally URL-decodes (catching double-encoded %252e%252f traversal) and re-runs processPath before re-checking (lines 116-135, 194-236); this blocks the classic /{name}/{profile}/{label}/../../.. traversal that CVE-2019-3799-style requests rely on, and the checks are present (not reverted) in this snapshot. Paths of exactly ".." or "a/.." collapse via cleanPath to "" or "a" and pass the check but only resolve to directories, which cannot be streamed as files. Spring's UrlPathHelper collapses duplicate slashes and path parameters, and a real servlet container (Tomcat) normalizes/rejects raw "../" segments, so the traversal must be delivered through the label (including the "(_)" substitution) rather than through the path variable. Exploitability is therefore configuration-dependent (native/SVN backends or {label} in search paths), and the environment endpoint is further limited to config-named files. These conditions reduce, but do not eliminate, the impact; the location-building code contains no equivalent validation at all.
candidates.impact: Directory traversal / arbitrary file disclosure from the config-server filesystem (configuration files containing credentials, and any file readable by the server process when the attacker controls the searched directory), i.e. sensitive information exposure and a stepping stone for further compromise. No code execution is demonstrated.
candidates.prerequisites: Config server endpoints reachable by the attacker (they are ordinary MVC endpoints; the repo provides no authentication of its own). Traversal effect is configuration-dependent: clearest with the native backend (spring.profiles.active=native; spring.cloud.config.server.native.add-label-locations defaults to true), or with the subversion profile (SvnKitEnvironmentRepository), or with a git/SCM backend whose search paths contain the {label} placeholder. Server filesystem must contain the target directory and, for the environment endpoint, a config-named file matching <application>[-<profile>].{properties,yml,yaml} for the requested names.
candidates.root_cause: Attacker-controlled label reaches filesystem location/file construction without the traversal validation that is applied to the resource path. ResourceController.getFilePath extracts the path after the stem but the label itself is never validated; ResourceController.resolveLabel/EnvironmentController.labelled expand "(_)" to "/", so a single URL segment can carry directory separators plus ".." segments that never appear as standalone "../" in the raw request line. NativeEnvironmentRepository.getLocations then appends the label to every search location (addLabelLocations defaults to true), and SvnKitEnvironmentRepository.getSvnPath builds new File(workingDirectory, label) from the label. GenericResourceRepository only calls isInvalidPath/isInvalidEncodedPath on the *relative* path relative to those locations, so traversal contained in the location itself is never checked.
candidates.title: Directory traversal via unvalidated label used to build repository search locations/paths (CWE-22 file disclosure)
candidates.trace: HTTP GET -> ResourceController.retrieve/labelled gets name/profile/label from the URL; resolveLabel/EnvironmentController.labelled replace "(_)" with "/"; GenericResourceRepository.findOne(name, profile, label, path) calls service.getLocations(application, profile, label) (line 64) -> NativeEnvironmentRepository.getLocations appends location + label.trim() + "/" for every configured search location (lines 194-203) after only isDirectory() string-suffix filtering -> locations outside the configured roots (e.g. file:./config/../../../.. /etc/) are returned; the relative path is then validated (line 70) but the location is not -> resourceLoader.getResource(location).createRelative(local) opens the file (lines 71-74) and ResourceController streams it back. With the SVN backend the same label reaches SvnKitEnvironmentRepository.getSvnPath (new File(workingDirectory, label), lines 191-199) and the resulting directory is used as the search location; EnvironmentController.labelled feeds the same label through repository.findOne.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. I did not execute the server or craft requests; exploitability depends on the active repository backend configuration (native profile with add-label-locations, subversion profile, or git search paths containing {label}) and on servlet-container/Spring MVC path-decoding behavior that cannot be fully resolved by static reading. The exact upstream CVE/patch identity for this snapshot was not determined (no patch, metadata, CVE or external data was consulted).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 160-file source tree (spring-cloud-config 2.1.6.RELEASE modules: server, client, monitor, starter, sample, build files). I listed all files and performed targeted text searches (path/sanitization/exec/deserialization/TLS/logging patterns), then read in depth the HTTP controllers (EnvironmentController, ResourceController, EncryptionController, monitor PropertyPathEndpoint/FileMonitorConfiguration), the repository implementations (GenericResourceRepository, Native, JGit, MultipleJGit, SvnKit, Vault, Credhub, Jdbc, composite), configuration/auto-configuration, the SSH validators/transport callbacks, encryption helpers, and the client locator. Tests and most documentation are not part of the assigned tree, so verification relies on source only.
limitations: No code was executed; findings are static and not runtime-confirmed.

Exploitability of the label-based traversal depends on the active backend configuration (native profile with add-label-locations default true, subversion profile, or git search paths containing {label}); a default git-profile deployment with default search paths does not appear to traverse.

Servlet-container behavior (Tomcat URI normalization, rejection of escaping '..' segments, encoded-slash handling) and Spring MVC UrlPathHelper decoding could not be verified by execution; the '(_)'-to-'/' substitution is the mechanism that survives those layers in the analyzed code.
The intended ground-truth CVE/patch for this case could not be identified from the snapshot alone (no patches, CVE labels, or external data were consulted, per instructions).

Environment endpoint disclosure is constrained to config-file naming patterns (<application>[-<profile>].{properties,yml,yaml}); the resource endpoint can serve arbitrary filenames once the location is attacker-influenced.

No test sources or runtime configuration of a real deployment were available, so authentication/authorization in front of the config server (e.g. Spring Security or a proxy) is out of scope and could mitigate reachability.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal through the ResourceController resource path itself (the classic /{name}/{profile}/{label}/..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd request)
rejected_leads.reason: GenericResourceRepository already validates the relative path with isInvalidPath and isInvalidEncodedPath (including a URLDecoder pass that catches double-encoded sequences) and processPath normalization, matching Spring Framework's ResourceHttpRequestHandler hardening; no live bypass was established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: EnvironmentController '(_)'-based name/label rewriting as an injection into git checkout / multiple-repo URI placeholders
rejected_leads.reason: The rewritten label does reach git checkout and MultipleJGitEnvironmentRepository URI substitution, but JGit ref validation and the fixed configured URI make a concrete security impact (file read / SSRF) speculative; only the search-location/SVN file-path sinks give a clear filesystem effect.

rejected_leads.lead: VaultEnvironmentRepository using the request X-Config-Token header and X-Config-State header
rejected_leads.reason: Passing a client-provided Vault token through to Vault is documented intended behavior; the token is not logged and remains scoped to the configured Vault host.

rejected_leads.lead: AwsCodeCommitCredentialProvider logging access key/session data and derived password at TRACE level (get(), lines 315-331), and GitCredentialsProviderFactory fallback to DefaultAWSCredentialsProviderChain
rejected_leads.reason: The logging is TRACE-gated and not attacker-influenced; the default credentials chain is an intended fallback for CodeCommit URIs.

rejected_leads.lead: SSH host-key handling (PropertyBasedSshSessionFactory.configure disabling StrictHostKeyChecking when hostKey is absent; FileBasedSshTransportConfigCallback toggling it)
rejected_leads.reason: The behavior matches the documented strictHostKeyChecking/hostKey properties and the associated JSR-303 validators; no missing check or inversion relative to the surrounding property contract was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Synthetic/injected-bug search across the tree (Class.forName in CompositeUtils, JDBC SQL in JdbcEnvironmentRepository, HttpClientSupport SSL/proxy handling)
rejected_leads.reason: CompositeUtils.forName uses Spring bean metadata return types, not request data; JdbcEnvironmentRepository uses a parameterized JdbcTemplate.query with bound app/profile/label; HttpClientSupport only skips TLS validation when explicitly configured via isSkipSslValidation().

summary: The snapshot is spring-cloud-config 2.1.6.RELEASE (server, client, monitor; 160 visible main-source files; tests/docs are not present in the assigned tree). HTTP entry points are EnvironmentController and ResourceController, both fed by attacker-controlled path segments (name, profile(s), label). The repository code hardens the *relative resource path* against traversal (GenericResourceRepository.isInvalidPath / isInvalidEncodedPath, mirrored from Spring's ResourceHttpRequestHandler), but the *label* (and, where configured, application/profile) is used to build filesystem search locations and filesystem paths with no equivalent validation, and ResourceController/EnvironmentController additionally rewrite "(_)" to "/" inside the label. The strongest evidence-supported issue is therefore a path-traversal/arbitrary-file-disclosure chain in which an attacker who can reach the config-server endpoints and influence the label can cause the server to search and serve files outside the configured locations (native backend, SVN backend, or a git backend whose search paths use {label}). I could not verify which upstream security patch (if any) the case corresponds to; no runtime confirmation was performed and no patch/metadata was consulted.
